mode_evidence: Wenger's target is imagery in the 'mind's eye' described aloud; he even says to describe it 'as if you were still looking at it' and allows made-up detail to start the flow. But his starters (afterimage, phosphenes, strobe, light flicks, blobs of colour) are seen light, and he claims afterimages sustained by describing lasted long minutes, in one case 4 hours.
onset_evidence: Built for people who see nothing: 24 back-up procedures, each tried 10 to 20 minutes; claims no one has gone through them without getting pictures. Entry via helper partner who watches breath pauses and eye movements under lids and asks 'What was in your awareness just then?'; via afterimage; via reporting blobs of colour then looking beyond them as through a screen; via phosphenes from rubbing closed eyes. Time scale: minutes to hours per session. No grace claim; he says the ability is natural.

conditions.gaze_or_eye_position: eyes closed throughout; look beyond colour as beyond a screen
conditions.setting: dark room for flicker starters; a listener or tape recorder
conditions.duration_and_schedule: 10 to 30 minutes per session; 10 to 20 minutes per starter before switching
conditions.prerequisites: a live listener or recorder to describe to; strobe only if not epileptic
conditions.other: describe rapidly in sensory detail, present tense, without judging

stages.label: afterimage or blobs of colour
stages.description: described continuously as it changes colour and shape

stages.label: other image
stages.description: a face, eye, landscape or vase appears; switch to describing it

what_to_do_with_light: describe it aloud continuously and richly; when something else appears switch to that; look beyond the colour
obstacles_and_fixes: no pictures: move through the back-up procedures
afterimage fades: recharge on a 20 to 40 watt light and resume
feeling of forcing or making up: allowed at the start
cautions: do not stare at anything near sun brightness
interpretation: Images are messages from subtler faculties, often symbolic; the afterimage is mainly a bridge, not the goal.
practice_summary: Close the eyes and describe aloud, to a listener or tape recorder, whatever appears, rapidly and in sensory detail, in present tense. If nothing comes, stare half a minute at a modest light (20 to 40 watts) or a contrasty window, close the eyes and describe the afterimage as it changes, recharging when it fades. Or report any blobs, lines or patterns however trivial, and after some minutes look beyond them as through a screen. Or rub the closed eyes gently and describe the phosphenes. Flick lights on and off with eyes closed, or use a strobe at 4 to 12 beats per second if not epileptic. Sessions run 10 to 30 minutes. Keep the description flowing; new images arrive as you describe, and a partner can spot eye movements under the lids.
